newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale asked to testify in CWB court case - defence.
newsitem.headline: Goodale asked to testify in CWB court case - defence.

text.p: Canada Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale was asked Wednesday to testify in the defense of 14 Alberta farmers charged with shipping wheat and barley without Canadian Wheat Board export permits.
Goodale's spokesman, Vern Greenshields, was not immediately available for comment.
The farmers were charged in April under the same section of the Canada Customs Act as another farmer who was acquitted May 17 on a technicality, a defence press release said.
An hour after the acquittal, federal cabinet passed an order amending the CWB Act to correct the technicality.

"Since we were charged before the Minister created this regulation, how can the charge be sound? Since the regulation which the Minister amended were those under the CWB Act, why is he continuing to charge farmers under the Customs Act," the Canadian Farmers for Justice statement said.
CFJ is a farm group protesting mandatory wheat and barley sales through the CWB.
